title: What is the top of a pyramid with en rows?
description: A pyramid with en rows has the first en Virahanka Fibonacci numbers in its bottom row. Every row moves two places along the sequence, so every number is a sequence number and the top lies at place two en minus one.
teaching_notes: One idea: each row of the pyramid starts two places further along the sequence than the row below, so the top is en minus one steps of two places from the start. Watch for students who count en steps instead of en minus one.

video_script.why: The child uses a letter for the number of rows and finds where the top of the pyramid lies in the sequence, for every pyramid at once.
video_script.substitution: Count the steps up as en minus one, move two places for each, and start from place one.
video_script.anchor: a pyramid with n rows, with the first n sequence numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, ... in its bottom row
video_script.payoff_line: Every number is a sequence number, and the top is at place two en minus one.

final_answer.value: every number is a Virahanka-Fibonacci number; the top is at place 2n - 1
final_answer.spoken: every number is a sequence number, and the top is at place two en minus one

maths_rules: Two neighbours of the sequence add to the number two places on, so each row is a run of sequence numbers two places further along.
Bottom row starts at place 1; the top is n - 1 steps up, each step 2 places, so it is at place 1 + 2(n - 1) = 2n - 1.
Check: n = 3 gives place 5, the number 8; n = 4 gives place 7, the number 21.
video_script.design: One idea: each row moves two places along, and the top is en minus one rows above the bottom. The pyramid stays in the anchor band and the counting sits on the working board.
